topic: contingent self-worth and why approval doesn't relieve stress
title: Why Getting Approval Doesn't Fix The Stress It Was Supposed To
description: AI-narrated commentary on the psychology of contingent self-worth — why chasing others' approval doesn't actually relieve the anxiety behind it. #psychology #shorts #mentalhealth

hook_candidates.text: Some people's stress hormones spike **even when** they get the approval they were chasing.
Why does getting the compliment you wanted still leave you feeling **empty**?
Confidence isn't believing you're better than everyone else — it's not **needing** them to say so.
A psychologist once tracked students' stress hormones on exam day — the ones chasing the grade for validation were just as stressed **after** acing it.

beats.text: Some people's stress hormones spike **even when** they get the approval they were chasing.
Psychologists call it **contingent** self-worth — worth that depends on someone else's reaction.
That's why the spike never stops — approval doesn't pay it off, it just **resets** the bill. What's yours?
